raw_response:
I farm this land the way I always have to think about it: first make sure the family does not lose too much money, then see if there is still something left to earn. I am already old, only two of us are at home, so I cannot spread myself too thin. On my better and more convenient land, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the surest way here in Quzhou. Wheat gives me one harvest, then maize follows right after, and even if one side is not so good, the other can help. I will leave about 6.1 mu for cotton, because cotton can still bring cash, but it needs more hand work, so I do not want too much of it. I do not read books or count fancy formulas. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and whether I can afford the fertilizer and water. If the crop looks weak, I will add a bit; if money is tight, I would rather keep the plan simple than chase a big yield and get stuck with debt.
